All four rows (P6022/P6023/P6024/P6025) trace to ONE source. Decide whether P6024 should survive as a discrete GGIT row at all, or be folded into the Esfarayen-Neqab-Joghatai cluster / dropped as a small feeder.
validity.researcher_notes: The row's ONLY support (both on the sheet and in the gem.wiki outbound citations) is a single Iran Ertebat project page, 'construction-of-reinforcing-gas-pipeline-transmission-in-esfarayen-neghab-joghtay'. That page does NOT name an 'Esfarayen Gas Pipeline' as a discrete asset — it describes the Esfarayen-Neqab-Joghatai REINFORCEMENT project (a NEW 30-inch + 20-inch, ~70 km transmission line in Razavi Khorasan, built to feed the Sabzevar steel plant AND to 'strengthen the existing 10-inch branch of Esfarayen city'). That single page is the shared, sole citation for FOUR ProjectIDs at once: P6022 (30in/48km), P6023 (20in/35km), P6024 (this row, 10in), and P6025 (Sabzevar steel spur, 12in) — confirmed by reading wiki_citations.json (identical iranertebat URL on all four). So P6024 is not the reinforcement line itself; it is the small PRE-EXISTING 10-inch city branch (Persian: 'انشعاب موجود شهر اسفراین') that the project merely mentions in passing. Independent search corroborates that a ~10-inch gas line exists in the Esfarayen/North-Khorasan area (news of an excavator strike on a 10-inch, 800-850 PSI gas transmission line in the Bojnord/Esfarayen district; Iran Ertebat + FSEC consulting both reference the reinforcement project), so this is NOT a pure phantom — but there is NO independent source that names or documents 'Esfarayen Gas Pipeline' as a standalone named transmission pipeline. Per the existence rubric (sole cited source does not name the line; no independent naming) this is an existence/documentation flag. Not a strict 1:1 duplicate of another PID (P6022/P6023 are the distinct 30in/20in new-build, P6025 the 12in steel spur), but the whole P6022-P6025 cluster is one project fragmented into four rows. GulfPub PE World Map (49 Iran gas features) has NO counterpart for any Esfarayen/Neqab/Joghatai line — its Iran roster jumps straight from IGAT/cross-border trunks and offshore lines with nothing in this small North-Khorasan feeder class, consistent with P6024 being below the trunk-transmission tier. Could not machine-verify any URL: the iranertebat page ConnectTimeouts from this environment (dead/unreachable), and Persian news pages (Shana, IRNA, snn, yjc) are JS-rendered so url_verifier cannot confirm the token even at HTTP 200. No fabricated ref supplied.

validity.recommendation: Fix province and owner: StartState/Province should be North Khorasan (خراسان شمالی), not Razavi Khorasan — Esfarayen city is in North Khorasan. Owner should be a National Iranian Gas Company entity (NIGC / North Khorasan Provincial Gas Co), not National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC), for a domestic city gas branch. Also review FuelSource='Esfarayen' — Esfarayen is the DESTINATION city, not a gas source field/plant.
validity.researcher_notes: Province: the sheet puts StartState/Province='Razavi Khorasan', but Esfarayen (اسفراین) is a city in NORTH Khorasan Province, ~37.08N 57.51E. The Razavi-Khorasan label belongs to the reinforcement line's Neqab/Joghatai/Sabzevar end (P6022/P6023/P6025), not to the 10-inch Esfarayen branch — a province mis-carry from the shared source. Owner: Owner1='National Iranian Oil Co' (NIOC) is implausible for a small domestic city gas branch; Iran's domestic gas transmission/distribution is NIGC and its provincial subsidiaries (here North Khorasan Gas Co). GulfPub records comparable small Iranian domestic gas lines (Iranshahr-Zahedan, Sarkhun-Kerman) under 'National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC)', supporting NIGC over NIOC. FuelSource='Esfarayen' is a destination city, not a gas source, so the FuelSource field is also suspect. These are attribution fixes contingent on the row surviving the existence/merge review above. Values not independently machine-verifiable (see existence note); flagged as deliberate GEM divergences to verify, not overwrite.

routes.corridor_desc: Loosely bounded. This row is the small pre-existing 10-inch gas branch serving Esfarayen city in North Khorasan (well-established city location, ~37.08N 57.51E). Its second endpoint is a tie-in on the regional gas transmission network and is NOT precisely documented for the 10-inch line specifically. The associated reinforcement project (P6022 30in / P6023 20in, ~70 km) runs southeast out of the Esfarayen area across the North-Khorasan / Razavi-Khorasan boundary through the Neqab-Joghatai area toward Sabzevar (feeding the Sabzevar steel plant, P6025). The tightest defensible corridor is the Esfarayen -> Joghatai/Neqab -> Sabzevar axis (~37.08N,57.51E down to ~36.21N,57.68E), but which portion the 10-inch branch occupies vs. the 20/30-inch reinforcement line cannot be separated from available sources.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoint coordinates are real, well-known city locations (Esfarayen, Joghatai/Neqab, Sabzevar), used as defensible anchors — NOT surveyed pipeline coordinates and NOT fabricated. No route GeoJSON or coordinate list for the 10-inch Esfarayen branch could be sourced or machine-verified (iranertebat page unreachable; Persian news JS-rendered). Suggestion only; do not auto-apply. If the existence/merge review folds P6024 into the Esfarayen-Neqab-Joghatai cluster, route work should be done on that consolidated entity.

summary: P6024 'Esfarayen Gas Pipeline' = the pre-existing 10-inch Esfarayen city branch mentioned only in passing by the one shared source (iranertebat) that also feeds P6022/P6023/P6025; no independent source names it as a discrete pipeline -> existence/fragmentation concern, plus attribution errors (province should be North Khorasan not Razavi Khorasan; owner likely NIGC not NIOC).
